blocks.text: In an engine, the connecting rod swings and slides at once, so no point on it has simple circular motion. Yet at any instant there is one point about which the whole rod is turning, and finding it turns a messy vector problem into a single division. This unit applies that point to four-bar linkages and slider-cranks.

blocks.markdown: For a body in plane motion, the **instantaneous centre of rotation** (IC) is the point with zero velocity at that instant. Every other point moves as if the body were rotating about it, so $v=\omega\,d$, where $d$ is the distance from the IC. For two bodies $i$ and $j$ in a mechanism, the **relative IC** $I_{ij}$ is the point that has the same velocity in both. For a mechanism with $n$ links the number of ICs is $n(n-1)/2$; a four-bar has 6 and a slider-crank also has 6.

blocks.title: Aronhold-Kennedy theorem
blocks.text: Any three bodies in relative plane motion have their three relative instantaneous centres on one straight line. For links 1, 2 and 3 this means $I_{12}$, $I_{23}$ and $I_{13}$ are collinear. The theorem lets you locate ICs that are not visible as pins.

blocks.markdown: **Obvious ICs.** A pin joining two links is their IC. A sliding joint has its IC at infinity, perpendicular to the sliding direction. In a four-bar with ground 1, crank 2, coupler 3 and rocker 4: $I_{12}=O_2$, $I_{23}=A$, $I_{34}=B$ and $I_{14}=O_4$. The other two follow from the theorem.

blocks.caption: $I_{13}$ is the intersection of the lines $O_2A$ and $O_4B$; $I_{24}$ is the intersection of the ground line $O_2O_4$ and the coupler line $AB$.

blocks.markdown: **Using the IC.** $I_{13}$ is a point common to the coupler and the ground, so the coupler is turning about it. The coupler angular velocity is $\omega_3=v_A/\overline{AI_{13}}$ and any other point on the coupler has speed $\omega_3\times$ (distance to $I_{13}$).

blocks.title: Coupler of a four-bar
blocks.prompt: $O_2=(0,0)$, $O_4=(0.4,0)$ m. The crank $O_2A$ is vertical with $A=(0,0.1)$ m and turns counterclockwise at $\omega_2=10$ rad/s. The coupler is horizontal with $B=(0.3,0.1)$ m. Find $\omega_3$ and $\omega_4$.

steps.text: Locate $I_{13}$: line $O_2A$ is $x=0$; line $O_4B$ passes through $(0.4,0)$ and $(0.3,0.1)$ so $y=0.4-x$. They meet at $(0,0.4)$ m.
Speed of $A$ is $\omega_2\,O_2A=10(0.1)=1.0$ m/s. Distances from $I_{13}$: $AI_{13}=0.30$ m.

blocks.markdown: **Slider-crank.** For crank $O_2A$ of length $r$, connecting rod $AB$ of length $l$ and a slider $B$ moving along the $x$-axis, $I_{14}$ is at infinity in the vertical direction, so $I_{13}$ is where the vertical line through $B$ meets the line $O_2A$ extended. The rod turns about $I_{13}$ and the slider speed is $v_B=\omega_3\,\overline{BI_{13}}$.

blocks.title: Slider velocity at a crank angle
blocks.prompt: A slider-crank has $r=0.10$ m, $l=0.40$ m and $\omega_2=100$ rad/s. Find the slider speed when the crank is $60^\circ$ above the line of stroke.

steps.text: $I_{13}$ on the vertical through $B$: $\overline{BI_{13}}=x_B\tan60^\circ=0.7630$ m; $\overline{O_2I_{13}}=x_B/\cos60^\circ=0.8810$ m so $\overline{AI_{13}}=0.7810$ m.

rows: Intersection of ground line $O_2O_4$ and coupler line $AB$
blocks.caption: Instantaneous centres of a four-bar linkage.

blocks.title: Why it saves work
blocks.text: Velocity analysis reduces to measuring distances to the right IC. $I_{24}$ also gives the velocity ratio: $\omega_4/\omega_2=\overline{I_{24}I_{12}}/\overline{I_{24}I_{14}}$, positive when $I_{24}$ lies outside the segment $O_2O_4$.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.text: Measuring from the wrong IC (the coupler turns about $I_{13}$, not about $A$), forgetting that parallel lines place an IC at infinity (so the link translates), and using $I_{13}$ distances on the slider instead of on the rod.

points: The IC is the zero-velocity point of a body at an instant; speeds are $\omega d$ about it.
Aronhold-Kennedy: three relative ICs of any three bodies are collinear; this finds $I_{13}$ and $I_{24}$.
For a four-bar $\omega_3=v_A/\overline{AI_{13}}$; for a slider-crank the slider speed is $\omega_3\,\overline{BI_{13}}$.

questions.stem: How many instantaneous centres of rotation exist for a planar mechanism with 6 links (including the frame)?

distractorRationale.a: This is the number of links, not the number of pairs.
distractorRationale.d: This counts ordered pairs $n(n-1)$, double counting each IC.

questions.explanation: Each pair of links has one relative IC, so the count is $n(n-1)/2=6\cdot5/2=15$. A four-bar ($n=4$) has 6.

questions.stem: Which statement is the Aronhold-Kennedy theorem?

options.text: The instantaneous centre of a body always lies at its centre of mass
Any three instantaneous centres of a mechanism are at the vertices of an equilateral triangle
Three bodies in relative plane motion have their three relative instantaneous centres on one straight line
Two links connected by a pin have their instantaneous centre at infinity

questions.correctOptionText: Three bodies in relative plane motion have their three relative instantaneous centres on one straight line

distractorRationale.a: The IC is generally unrelated to the centre of mass.
distractorRationale.b: The theorem concerns collinearity, not geometry of a triangle.
distractorRationale.d: A pin is the IC; infinity is for sliding joints.

questions.explanation: For bodies $i$, $j$, $k$ the centres $I_{ij}$, $I_{jk}$, $I_{ik}$ are collinear. This is the tool for locating non-obvious centres such as $I_{13}$ and $I_{24}$.

questions.stem: In a four-bar, the crank $O_2A$ is 0.12 m long and turns at 8 rad/s. The extended lines of $O_2A$ and the rocker $O_4B$ meet at $I_{13}$, which lies 0.30 m beyond $A$ on line $O_2A$ and 0.42 m from $B$ on the coupler; the rocker is $O_4B=0.28$ m long. Using instantaneous centres, find the rocker's angular velocity magnitude in rad/s.

A slider-crank has crank $r=0.08$ m and connecting rod $l=0.32$ m. The crank turns at 150 rad/s and is perpendicular to the line of stroke ($\theta=90^\circ$). Using the instantaneous centre of the rod, find the slider speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: At $\theta=90^\circ$ the line $O_2A$ and the vertical through the slider are parallel, so $I_{13}$ is at infinity and the rod is in instantaneous translation. Then $v_B=v_A=\omega r=150(0.08)=12$ m/s.

questions.stem: A slider-crank has $r=0.10$ m, $l=0.40$ m, crank speed 60 rad/s, and the crank is $45^\circ$ from the line of stroke. Find the slider speed in m/s.
questions.explanation: The rod's instantaneous centre is on the vertical through the slider. The slider position is $x_B=0.0707+\sqrt{0.16-0.005}=0.4644$ m, $\overline{BI_{13}}=x_B\tan45^\circ=0.4644$ m and $\overline{AI_{13}}=x_B/\cos45^\circ-r=0.5568$ m. Then $v_B=60(0.10)(0.4644)/0.5568=5.00$ m/s.

questions.stem: At a certain instant the instantaneous centre $I_{13}$ of the coupler of a four-bar lies at infinity. What does this imply?

options.text: The coupler has zero angular velocity and is in instantaneous translation

questions.correctOptionText: The coupler has zero angular velocity and is in instantaneous translation

distractorRationale.b: All points translate with the same velocity, which is not necessarily zero.
distractorRationale.c: An IC at infinity means no rotation, not infinite rotation.
distractorRationale.d: The rocker speed is set by the crank speed and geometry, not by the IC being at infinity.

questions.explanation: When $I_{13}$ is at infinity every point of the coupler has the same velocity, i.e. $\omega_3=0$. This occurs when $O_2A$ and $O_4B$ are parallel.

questions.stem: In the Aronhold-Kennedy construction for a four-bar, which three centres lie on one line together with $I_{13}$?

distractorRationale.a: These are $O_2$ and $B$, which do not both belong to links 1, 2, 3.
distractorRationale.b: These are $O_4$ and $A$, which do not both belong to links 1, 2, 3.
distractorRationale.c: These involve link 4, which is not part of the triple (1, 2, 3).

questions.explanation: The triple (1, 2, 3) has centres $I_{12}$, $I_{23}$ and $I_{13}$, which are collinear, so $I_{13}$ lies on the line through $O_2$ and $A$.

questions.stem: In a four-bar with ground 1, crank 2, coupler 3 and rocker 4, which two lines intersect at $I_{24}$?

options.text: The ground line $O_2O_4$ and the coupler line $AB$, both extended

questions.correctOptionText: The ground line $O_2O_4$ and the coupler line $AB$, both extended

distractorRationale.c: These meet at the pin $A$, which is $I_{23}$.
distractorRationale.d: These meet at the pin $B$, which is $I_{34}$.

questions.explanation: For links 2, 3, 4, $I_{24}$ lies on $I_{23}I_{34}$, which is line $AB$. For links 1, 2, 4 it lies on $I_{12}I_{14}$, the line $O_2O_4$. The intersection of these two lines locates $I_{24}$.

questions.stem: Explain how the instantaneous centre of the coupler of a four-bar linkage is found, and how it is then used to obtain the coupler angular velocity and the speed of the other pin $B$ when the crank speed is known.
markingGuide: Locates $I_{13}$ as the intersection of lines $O_2A$ and $O_4B$
Gets $v_B=\omega_3\,\overline{BI_{13}}$ and $\omega_4=v_B/O_4B$, noting directions are perpendicular to the lines to $I_{13}$
questions.explanation: $I_{13}$ is the point where the coupler's velocity is zero relative to the ground, so the coupler turns about it at that instant. Velocities of $A$ and $B$ are perpendicular to their lines to $I_{13}$, which also fixes the senses.

questions.stem: For a slider-crank mechanism (frame 1, crank 2, rod 3, slider 4), state the Aronhold-Kennedy theorem and use it to locate $I_{13}$. Explain what happens to the rod's motion when the crank is at top dead centre.
markingGuide: States collinearity of three relative centres of any three bodies
Notes $I_{12}=O_2$, $I_{23}=A$, $I_{34}=B$ and $I_{14}$ at infinity perpendicular to the stroke
$I_{13}$ lies on the line through $I_{12}$ and $I_{23}$ (line $O_2A$) and on the line through $I_{14}$ and $I_{34}$ (vertical through $B$)
Takes the intersection of the two lines as $I_{13}$
At top dead centre $O_2A$ and the stroke line coincide so $I_{13}$ falls on the line of stroke at $B$, giving zero slider velocity
questions.explanation: At dead centre the vertical through $B$ meets the crank line at $B$ itself, so $\overline{BI_{13}}=0$ and $v_B=\omega_3\cdot0=0$. The slider reverses direction there.
